summary: CLI command routing and execution — entry point for `find`, `gs`, `index`, `consumers`, and `kb`. Key pattern: runGs calls ensureKeeper before the cache load (keeps the index fresh for uncommitted edits) while runConsumers loads the cache directly with no keeper (pure read for capture hooks); the choice turns on whether the command needs live freshness. runGs also loads the co-change sidecar itself and passes it into handleGetStructure — reader-side, because handleGetStructure cannot reach disk. parseQueryArgs is a flat switch over every flag any subcommand accepts, so a flag added for one command is silently accepted by all of them; removing a command means removing its flags here too or they linger as dead accepted input.

summary: CLI command routing and execution — entry point for `find`, `gs`, `index`, `consumers`, and `kb`. runGs calls ensureKeeper before the cache load (keeps the index fresh for uncommitted edits) while runConsumers loads the cache directly with no keeper (pure read for capture hooks). runGs also loads the co-change sidecar itself and passes it into handleGetStructure, because handleGetStructure cannot reach disk. runFind's internal flags for the injection hook: --embed-stdin reads the FULL user prompt from stdin as the re-rank query (stdin, not argv: Windows caps a command line at 32k chars) and --rerank-budget-ms widens the query-embed budget; both pass to buildRichPage's opts with flags.cacheDir. parseQueryArgs is a flat switch over every flag any subcommand accepts, so a flag added for one command is silently accepted by all of them.
